why: A route page describes an approach couloir with snow, a short ice crux and a snow bowl to the summit, but a trip report places the start near the Bend Glacier, so crevasse exposure is not ruled out.
No page describing this gully turned up; its own text puts it in the winter snow season.
A route page describes a ridge of moderate snow needing crampons and axe, approached from the PCT, and says nothing about a glacier either way.
A climbing journal report describes an ice runnel, snow gullies and a couloir reached by walking through woods, and the peak's only glacier, on the north side, is documented as gone.
The old Lathrop Glacier on the north side is documented as completely melted to bare bedrock, so the glacier named in the approach is a remnant with no ice.
A route page describes easy ice in a gully, a snowfield and chimneys on the rock toe of Illumination Rock, with no glacier travel. Held at unsure in review: the no rested on absence of evidence.
The area page describes a low, shaded face by a highway with ice and steep snow couloirs, far below any Oregon glacier.
The area page describes rhyodacite pinnacles at about 3,400 ft in the Menagerie Wilderness, so the crevasse mentioned is a rock crack. Held at unsure in review: the no rested on absence of evidence.
Search snippets mention crevasses on neighbouring Jefferson glacier lines and a Jefferson Park Glacier variation, and no page I could read separated this ridge from them.
Search snippets call it a gully on firm snow with a small glacier lobe near the top, and I could not read a page settling it.

A route page says the climb has no crevasse crossings and follows a rock spur then a steep snow chute.
Trip reports describe a winter ice pillar and buttress, but common approaches pass the Hayden or Collier glaciers, and no page I could read settled it.

A route page describes moderate snow into runnels below the Steel Cliffs and does not mention crevasses, but it does not rule out glacier ground nearby.
